actions.title: Add repository-owned request planning composition
actions.desired_outcome: SAGE request execution derives required capabilities, eligible registered component candidates, selection evidence, and capability-gap decisions through a reusable repository-owned planning composition instead of requiring external helpers or callers to invent component-selection semantics.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned repository-owned planning composition accepts the literal request, resolved repository authority, and registered workflow-primitives catalog as its authoritative inputs.

The composition derives required capabilities and eligible component candidates from repository-owned contracts and metadata rather than requiring callers to author candidate selection_factors or reconstruct ComponentCandidate semantics.
Existing component.select remains the selection authority and unresolved or novel capabilities are routed through the existing capability.gap primitive before repository mutation.
Request execution consumes the planning result through a stable published interface so a normal request-execution proposal does not need externally invented candidate semantics.
A deterministic positive regression reproduces the semantic-vocabulary replay case and resolves its existing repository capabilities without external SAGE-construction logic.
A deterministic negative regression supplies a genuinely unsupported capability, produces an explicit capability-gap receipt, and blocks mutation.
Interface, schema, and evidence-placement contracts are validated before proposal execution so semantic, interface, or receipt-shape assumptions cannot be learned only by failed mutation attempts.

Tracked downloaded helpers and external callers are prohibited from reimplementing capability derivation, candidate eligibility, component selection, or capability-gap semantics when the planning composition applies.
measurement_plan: Measure the next ten request-execution planning events and report the percentage whose capabilities and candidates were derived by the repository-owned composition.
Require zero external-helper reconstructions of RequiredCapability, ComponentCandidate, selection_factors, or capability-gap decisions for covered request-execution workflows.
Track capability gaps detected before proposal generation and distinguish valid novel-capability gaps from planner or metadata defects.
Track first-pass request-execution planning success, component-selection failures, retries, and avoidable rework before and after adoption.
Do not claim improved SAGE semantic planning until measured executions show reduced planner-related retries or rework without suppressing valid capability gaps.

actions.title: Separate checkpoint persistence from promotion validation
actions.desired_outcome: SAGE treats repository commit and push as durable engineering-state persistence, not as an assertion that the persisted state is validated or promotable. Explicitly non-promotable work/checkpoint branches may preserve incomplete, temporarily invalid, or dependency-blocked states through frequent small commits and pushes for business continuity, while promotion across trust boundaries remains fail-closed until the complete applicable composite validation gate is satisfied.
acceptance_criteria: Repository policy explicitly distinguishes checkpoint persistence from promotion: a checkpoint commit or push may preserve incomplete or dependency-blocked work without asserting validation, merge readiness, activation readiness, or completion.
Checkpoint/work branches are explicitly non-authoritative and non-promotable until their complete applicable composite validation gate is satisfied.
Frequent small checkpoint commits and pushes are permitted and encouraged as a business-continuity control, including when final validation is blocked.

Clean-tree and exact-scope requirements remain in force where they protect atomic lifecycle transactions, registry mutations, promotion boundaries, and other operations whose semantics require a stable baseline.
Promotion to a higher-trust SAGE-compliant branch or main requires the conjunction of all applicable validation gates; checkpoint persistence alone can never satisfy or bypass a promotion gate.
SAGE-LESSON-20260728-005 is corrected so remote synchronization remains mandatory while validation-before-every-checkpoint is no longer encoded as a requirement.
Existing git.repository exact-scope commit/push mechanics are reused unless a repository-owned capability test proves a primitive-level extension is required.

A deterministic regression reproduces the SAGE-ACTION-20260807-001 / SAGE-ACTION-20260809-001 dependency deadlock and proves the valid path: preserve the incomplete state as a non-promotable checkpoint, govern and resolve the dependency, satisfy the complete composite gate, then permit promotion.
Checkpoint metadata or workflow receipts make promotion eligibility explicit and fail closed if an incomplete checkpoint is represented as validated or promotable.
measurement_plan: Track checkpoint commits created while validation is incomplete or dependency-blocked and verify that they remain non-promotable until their composite gate passes.
Track long-duration uncommitted-work incidents and require zero recurrence attributable to SAGE policy prohibiting safe checkpoint persistence.
Track promotion attempts from checkpoint branches and require zero successful promotions without all applicable validation gates satisfied.
Review the next ten checkpoint-to-promotion workflows for first-pass completion, business-continuity recovery, validation integrity, and unnecessary rework.
